references.text: Joshua sets up twelve stones after the Israelites cross the Jordan, recalling God's command in Deuteronomy to set up stones after crossing.
The stones set up at Gilgal after crossing the Jordan, as a fulfillment of the command to erect memorial stones.
Joshua builds an altar on Mount Ebal and writes the law on stones, directly fulfilling this command.
Earlier instructions concerning blessings and curses on Gerizim and Ebal, linked to the crossing of the Jordan.
Continuation of the instructions about the stones, including the altar on Mount Ebal and the inscription of the law.
The promise of the land that the Lord gives; the same language regarding God's gift of the land is used here.
Similar language about crossing the Jordan to take possession of the land that the Lord gives.
